newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia refocuses aid budget on poverty.
newsitem.headline: Australia refocuses aid budget on poverty.

text.p: Australia on Friday announced its A$1.5 billion (US$1.2 billion) foreign aid budget would focus on combatting poverty and not grand commercial projects.
Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said a review of the aid budget recommended a refocusing on humanitarian and economic targets in recipient nations.
"The committee's recommendation reafirms my strongly held view that aid should not be seen as a subsidy for business, nor as a mere extension of foreign policy objectives," Downer told reporters.

"The principle objectives of Australia's aid programme should be to ensure the reduction of poverty and the promotion of economic development as a permanent means of overcoming such poverty," Downer said.

Until now much of Australia's aid had dual aims -- to help foreign countries and advance Australian commercial interests. The former Labor government approved two bridges built by Australian firms across the Mekong River in Southeast Asia.
The aid report endorsed Australia's current focus on East Asia and the Pacific but recommended cutting the number of aid recipients from the current 60.
Australia's biggest aid recipient is Australia's nearest neighbour and former colony, Papua New Guinea, which gets more than A$300 million a year.
The report also called for the abandonment of Australia's long-standing but never-achieved aim of spending 0.7 percent of gross national product on aid. The current budget is about half.
The government cut aid spending in 1996/97 by 10 percent but calculates it is spending around the same as other middle-of-the-range developed countries.
